checks: Missing derivative gate fails; exact restoration.
cost: O(n) validation, two products and additions per coefficient, one final pair gate; O(1) scratch. Overflow rejection may do more work than the early gate.
description: Ascending coefficients; preserve finite input validation and recurrence order, then reject a nonfinite final value/derivative pair. Empty polynomial returns (0,0). Absorption preserves Result observations while changing rejection work.
forward: Ascending coefficients; preserve finite input validation and recurrence order, then reject a nonfinite final value/derivative pair. Empty polynomial returns (0,0). Absorption preserves Result observations while changing rejection work.
inverse: At x=0 value=c0 and derivative=c1; all higher coefficients remain free. [2,3,7] and [2,3,99] have identical outputs. With fixed degree and x, real fiber is intersection of two affine constraints; dependent constraints and f64 rounding require separate treatment.
limitations: Finite fixtures and partial syntax are not a general proof.
IEEE-754 no-trap/no-fast-math assumptions; no percentage guarantee.
